summary: Glacier NP two-story NPS cab, built 1934 (or 1935), burned in April 1963; no source describes what remains at the site today.

facts.design: Two-story frame cab on a mid-slope hillside half a mile north of the summit
facts.status_note: Burned by the National Park Service in April 1963

access.note: Inside Glacier National Park. No source describes the site today.

visit.trail_note: A December 2009 post on the Glacier National Park Chat forum asked about the old trail to the site; current trail condition is not in these sources.

events.note: Two-story frame cab. WillhiteWeb gives 1935 for the cab.
Panorama photographs taken from the site (July 26, 1935 per the Forest Lookouts page).
Trail to the lookout washed out by spring rains and rebuilt.
A 1949 guidebook briefly mentions the trail to the lookout, which was then in use.
Burned by the National Park Service in April; the Forest Lookouts page says it was no longer of use.

notes_for_editor: Build year disputed: 1934 (firelookout.com, Forest Lookouts, Montana History Portal) vs 1935 (WillhiteWeb). Story gives both; not resolved. The FFLA Montana list has a second row, 'Bear Mountain Point', with identical coordinates (48.93557, -113.75050) and the same 2-story cab, Gone; possible duplicate, not checked. Trail detail comes from a 2009 forum post, not an authority. No source describes remains at the site.
